realAlignment.warning: Descriptive annual trend only. Not a fish-kill prediction, not a 72-hour model, and not an advisory.

stationNames: Stn V - West Bay near Pasig River

realAlignment.method: Ordinary least squares with station fixed effects and a common linear year term; HC3 standard errors; 1,000-replicate cluster bootstrap by station.
realAlignment.caveat: The estimates describe annual station summaries. They do not use observation dates, do not establish causation, and do not predict fish kills.

reasons: Water quality is reported as annual station summaries, not dated observations.
Rainfall and wind are monthly station summaries, not daily or sub-daily series.
There are zero pre-event observations and zero usable 24-hour labels.
There is one reported event and no verified negative windows.
Station coordinates and an authoritative lake-zone crosswalk are absent.

events.location: Biñan and Pila, Laguna (Laguna de Bay)
events.losses: Approximately 500,000 fish reported dead in fish cages in Biñan (fisherman's estimate); in Barangay Linga, Pila, 60% of tilapia and 80% of bangus in cages were reported killed. No complete count.
events.cause: Green tide (freshwater algal bloom) causing oxygen deficiency/asphyxia; attributed to an LLDA senior science research specialist quoted in the article.
events.sourceTitle: Seasonal Fish Kill Incident Leaves Thousands of Unprofitable Commodity Fish in Laguna de Bay
events.datePrecision: Start dates exact for Biñan (4 May) and Pila (12 May); end date only described as 'until the end of May', so 31 May is an approximate boundary.
events.locationPrecision: Municipality-level for Biñan and Pila; one site named as Barangay Linga, Pila. No coordinates or lake-zone label are provided.
events.verification: Single institutional news report (UP Diliman) with named LLDA attribution and a water-quality table; not a formal LLDA investigation report and not independently corroborated in the supplied files.
events.notes: One article reports a fish kill across two municipalities during overlapping periods; it is retained as one event to avoid double-counting. The article's water sample was collected on 29 May 2019 (during/near the end of the event), not before it. Byline date is 10 June 2019; the page also shows a 13 June dateline. No peso loss or lake-zone designation is reported.

evidenceAudit.claim: Fish kills in Laguna de Bay were reported in the 1930s.
evidenceAudit.issue: No year, month, date, location within the lake, count, loss, or cause.
evidenceAudit.reason: Cannot form an event record or a label.

evidenceAudit.claim: From 1972 to 1998, 60% of Laguna de Bay fish-kill incidents were due to low dissolved oxygen; 80% occurred in May-September, mostly in the central arm and then the west arm.
evidenceAudit.issue: Aggregate statistics over 27 years; no individual event dates, counts, or losses.
evidenceAudit.reason: Aggregate statements must not be converted into invented event rows.

evidenceAudit.claim: Table 3 lists '2021 Jan. Laguna de Bay / Tilapia / Low DO levels [121]'.
evidenceAudit.issue: The row's cited source [121] is titled '2 Tons of Tilapia Lost as Fish Kill Hits Laguna's Sampaloc Lake'. Sampaloc Lake is a different waterbody.
evidenceAudit.reason: The table row and its citation conflict; do not count it as Laguna de Bay.

evidenceAudit.claim: Massive fish kill in Biñan and Pila, Laguna, starting 4 May and 12 May 2019, respectively, lasting until the end of May.
evidenceAudit.issue: One secondary source; two municipalities in one report; end date approximate; no lake-zone label or coordinates; environmental sample collected during event.
evidenceAudit.reason: Meets the minimum for a dated, located event record; verification limits are recorded.

readiness.requirement: At least two independent documented event periods for a chronological split
readiness.evidence: 1 event period(s); 1 accepted report(s); event years [2019]
readiness.consequence: Cannot place events in both training and test periods.

readiness.evidence: One institutional news report; no second source or formal LLDA/BFAR incident report supplied.
readiness.consequence: Event status is plausible but not independently verified.

readiness.requirement: Exact event start date for a 24-hour window
readiness.evidence: Biñan start 2019-05-04; Pila start 2019-05-12; end only approximate.
readiness.consequence: A start-day window is possible, but only for one event.

readiness.evidence: 0 rows have a full observation timestamp; 2,659 numeric annual station-year values exist.
readiness.consequence: No pre-event water-quality feature vector can be constructed.

readiness.requirement: A pre-event environmental match at a known lead time
readiness.evidence: 0 usable pre-event matches; the article sample is during-event.
readiness.consequence: No observation is known to have been available before the event.

readiness.requirement: Documented station coordinates and lake-zone mapping
readiness.evidence: 0 coordinates; 5/15 lake stations have a zone label in their name.
readiness.consequence: Events cannot be assigned to a station or zone defensibly.

readiness.requirement: Credible non-event windows with documented incident reporting
readiness.evidence: 135 annual station-years fall outside [2019], but there is no incident-reporting log to establish that no fish kill occurred.
readiness.consequence: Absence of a published report cannot be treated as a negative label.

readiness.evidence: 1 event period; no 24-hour negatives; class balance cannot be estimated.
readiness.consequence: Precision, recall and F1 would be undefined or meaningless.

readiness.requirement: A 24-hour prediction horizon supported by sampling frequency
readiness.evidence: Water quality is annual; weather is monthly. Neither resolves 24 hours.
readiness.consequence: The proposed 24-hour target is not supported.

readiness.requirement: Sufficient independent observations for chronological validation and a held-out period
readiness.evidence: One event period, one location pair, one event year.
readiness.consequence: No honest train/validation/test evaluation is possible.

risk.headline: No valid model prediction available
risk.summary: One reported event period, no pre-event daily observation, no credible negative windows, and no station-to-zone mapping.
reasons: LLDA water quality is published as annual station summaries.
PAGASA rainfall and wind are monthly station summaries.
The single accepted event report has no pre-event dated sample.
No station coordinates or authoritative zone map are supplied.
Absence of a fish-kill report is not a verified non-event.
